issues.note: Interlacing, filaments, warp and weft are far beyond B1 defining vocabulary.
Learner dictionaries commonly label this structural sense formal; the label is defensible.
It names Spanish and Portuguese, and it duplicates the entry-level note.
The field placement is debatable, and the contrast itself is accurate and useful.
Knitted and nonwoven materials are fabric too, so the woven-only definition is too narrow.
Fabric is not described as tall; this is an unnatural collocation.
The not-a-factory fact is repeated across several fields, against one fact, one field.
The building use is literal and mainly British, but a subsense or label may suffice.
The usage note restates the learner error and adaptation fact.
The building sense is historically older; the origin claim is false and misplaced.

findings.F1: The sense 1 definition uses technical words (interlacing, filaments, warp and weft) beyond a B1 learner.
findings.F2: The sense 1 false-friends adaptation note names specific languages and duplicates the entry-level note.
findings.F3: The sense 1 definition limits fabric to woven cloth, excluding knitted and nonwoven fabric.
findings.F5: The fact that fabric is not a factory is stated in several fields (usage note, learner error, two adaptation notes).
findings.F6: The core idea's 'from that' makes a false derivation claim outside the etymology field.
